evidence.title: Trolley park
evidence.text: In the United States, trolley parks, which started in the 19th century, were picnic and recreation areas along or at the ends of streetcar lines in most of the larger cities.

evidence.title: Trolley park
evidence.text: These were precursors to amusement parks.

evidence.title: Trolley park
evidence.text: These trolley parks were created by the streetcar companies to give people a reason to use their services on weekends.

evidence.title: Trolley park
evidence.text: These parks originally consisted of picnic groves and pavilions, and often held events such as dances, concerts and fireworks.

evidence.title: Trolley park
evidence.text: Many eventually added features such as swimming pools, carousels, Ferris wheels, roller coasters, sports fields, boats rides, restaurants and other resort facilities to become amusement parks. Various sources report the existence of between 1,500 and 2,000 amusement parks in the United States by 1919.

evidence.title: Knoebels Amusement Resort
evidence.text: Knoebels Amusement Resort ( ) is a family-owned and operated amusement park, picnic grove, and campground in Elysburg, Pennsylvania.

evidence.title: Knoebels Amusement Resort
evidence.text: It is and has been America's largest free-admission park for 90 years of operation.

evidence.title: Knoebels Amusement Resort
evidence.text: Opened in 1926, the park has more than 60 rides, three wooden roller coasters, one steel roller coaster, a 1913 carousel, and a haunted house dark ride that was featured on the Discovery Channel.

evidence.title: Knoebels Amusement Resort
evidence.text: The park and its rides have won awards from organizations such as "Amusement Today", American Coaster Enthusiasts, and the International Association of Amusement Parks and Attractions.

evidence.title: Knoebels Amusement Resort
evidence.text: In 2014, Travel Channel rated Knoebels one of their Top 10 Family Friendly Amusement Parks in the United States.

evidence.title: Knoebels Amusement Resort
evidence.text: America's Number One Amusement Park

evidence.title: Amusement park
evidence.text: An amusement park is a park that features various attractions, such as rides and games, as well as other events for entertainment purposes.

evidence.title: Amusement park
evidence.text: A theme park is a type of amusement park that bases its structures and attractions around a central theme, often featuring multiple areas with different themes.

evidence.title: Amusement park
evidence.text: Unlike temporary and mobile funfairs and carnivals, amusement parks are stationary and built for long-lasting operation.

evidence.title: Amusement park
evidence.text: They are more elaborate than city parks and playgrounds, usually providing attractions that cater to a variety of age groups.

evidence.title: Amusement park
evidence.text: While amusement parks often contain themed areas, theme parks place a heavier focus with more intricately-designed themes that revolve around a particular subject or group of subjects.

evidence.title: Joris Ivens
evidence.text: Georg Henri Anton "Joris" Ivens (18 November 1898 – 28 June 1989) was a Dutch documentary filmmaker.

evidence.title: Joris Ivens
evidence.text: Among the notable films he directed or co-directed are "A Tale of the Wind", "The Spanish Earth", "Rain", "...A Valparaiso", "Misère au Borinage" ("Borinage"), "", "The Seine Meets Paris", "Far from Vietnam", "Pour le Mistral" and "How Yukong Moved the Mountains".

evidence.title: Gay World Amusement Park
evidence.text: Located between Geylang Road and Grove Road (now Mountbatten Road), Gay World was one of the famous trio of "World" amusement parks in Singapore.

evidence.title: Gay World Amusement Park
evidence.text: Together with the other two "Worlds", Great World Amusement Park (1930s–1978) at Kim Seng Road and New World Amusement Park (1923–1987) at Jalan Besar, Gay World Park was hustling and bustling with nightlife during the 1930s to 1960s.

evidence.title: Gay World Amusement Park
evidence.text: These amusement parks were especially popular among Singaporeans as it was the locals only form of entertainment, before television or shopping malls were introduced.

evidence.title: Gay World Amusement Park
evidence.text: Gay World Park was an all-in-one complex, where visitors were offered a wide range of entertainment, from movies to shopping and games.

evidence.title: Gay World Amusement Park
evidence.text: However, as its popularity began to dip in the 1970s, Gay World Park was eventually demolished in 2000 to make way for residential estates.

evidence.title: Gay World Amusement Park
evidence.text: This officially marked the end of Gay World Park and its journey in the entertainment industry.

evidence.title: Great Old Amusement Parks
evidence.text: Great Old Amusement Parks is a 1999 PBS television documentary VHS by Rick Sebak of WQED Pittsburgh.

evidence.title: North Point State Park
evidence.text: North Point State Park is a public recreation area located on Chesapeake Bay in Edgemere, Baltimore County, Maryland.

evidence.title: North Point State Park
evidence.text: The state park includes the site of the former Bay Shore Park, which was one of the state's premiere amusement parks during the first half of the 20th century.

evidence.title: North Point State Park
evidence.text: The park features restored remnants of the old amusement park as well as facilities for swimming, picnicking, bicycling, and hiking.

evidence.title: North Point State Park
evidence.text: Black Marsh, a 667 acre state wildlands area, makes up half the park's area.

evidence.title: North Point State Park
evidence.text: The park is administered by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources.

evidence.title: The Seine Meets Paris
evidence.text: The Seine Meets Paris (French: La Seine a rencontré Paris ) is a 1957 French short documentary film directed by Joris Ivens from a screenplay by Jacques Prévert.

evidence.title: The Seine Meets Paris
evidence.text: Told from the perspective of a boat trip through the city, it features scenes of daily life along the river.

evidence.title: The Seine Meets Paris
evidence.text: The film won the short film Palme d'Or at the 1958 Cannes Film Festival.

evidence.title: List of amusement park rankings
evidence.text: Amusement parks and theme parks are terms for a group of entertainment attractions, rides, and other events in a location for the enjoyment of large numbers of people.

evidence.title: List of amusement park rankings
evidence.text: Amusement parks are located all around the world with millions of people visiting them every year.

evidence.title: List of amusement park rankings
evidence.text: This list of amusement park rankings summarizes the attendance records, park rankings and the results of public polls of amusement parks around the world.

evidence.title: Family entertainment center
evidence.text: A family entertainment center (or centre), often abbreviated FEC in the entertainment industry, (also known as indoor amusement park or indoor theme park) is a small amusement park marketed towards families with small children to teenagers, and often entirely indoors or associated with a larger operation such as a theme park.

evidence.title: Family entertainment center
evidence.text: They usually cater to "sub-regional markets of larger metropolitan areas."

evidence.title: Family entertainment center
evidence.text: FECs are generally small compared to full-scale amusement parks, with fewer attractions, a lower per-person per-hour cost to consumers than a traditional amusement park, and not usually major tourist attractions, but sustained by an area customer base.

evidence.title: Family entertainment center
evidence.text: Many are locally owned and operated, although there are a number of chains and franchises in the field.

evidence.title: Family entertainment center
evidence.text: FECs are sometimes called family amusement centers, play zones, family fun centers, or simply fun centers.

evidence.title: Family entertainment center
evidence.text: Some non-traditional FECs, called urban entertainment centers (UECs), with more customized and branded attractions and retail outlets, are associated with major entertainment companies and may be tourist destinations.

evidence.title: Family entertainment center
evidence.text: Others, sometimes operated by Non-Profit organizations as Children's Museums or Science Centers, tend to be geared toward edutainment experiences rather than simply amusement.

evidence.title: Family entertainment center
evidence.text: FECs may also be adjuncts to full-scale amusement parks.
